newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to threaten Spain over mobile phone fee.
newsitem.headline: EU to threaten Spain over mobile phone fee.

text.p: The European Commission is to use article 90 of the treaty to force Spain to correct what it says is unfair competition created by Madrid's decision to charge for a second mobile phone licence, an official said.
"The Commission is tired of waiting (for the Spanish government to propose a solution)," the Commission official said on Friday.

The official added that European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert had instructed his services to draft a decision under article 90 urging Spain to act quickly or face legal action. The decision could come as soon as mid November.

At issue is the payment by the Airtel consortium, which is led by U.S. company AirTouch Communications Inc, of a 85-billion-peseta fee for winning a licence to operate a second mobile phone service in Spain.
Partly state-owned telecoms operator Telefonica de Espana did not have to pay any such fee when it was given the first mobile phone licence.
The same situation happened in Italy, Belgium, Austria and Ireland when granting a second mobile phone licence.
The Commission cried foul each time and ordered that either the incumbent operator paid the same fee or that the newcomer be compensated.

Spanish Development Minister Rafael Arias Salgado told the Commission in July he was confident Airtel and Telefonica would reach a deal regarding, for example, the price and conditions for Airtel to interconnect with Telefonica's network.
But industry and Commission sources told Reuters that a deal was nowhere in sight.
The Commission can and has indeed used article 90 to ensure national monopolies or state-owned companies are not given preferential rights that would distort competition.
It has not been decided what legal form the article 90 decision will take, whether or not it will a directive, the source said.
